evals.protocol: Run the seven prompts in evals/cases.md as consecutive turns in one isolated session, explicitly invoking the named stage at each turn and withholding the assertions until grading.
evals.expected_output: A ready brief, cited report, explicitly accepted design and specification, a scoped planning research block resolved by withheld evidence, a ready plan and readiness assessment, then a Not Verified implementation report for the supplied 429 contract violation.
assertions: The brief is neutral and Ready, and its accepted Q identifiers are preserved in the research report.
The report stays descriptive, binds findings to w100, and passes only evidence plus the original change intent into design.
The design accepts only the human-selected options, records O/B/D/C identifiers and w100, and contains no specification or plan.
The accepted specification preserves O/B/D/C identifiers, adds traceable S identifiers, and contains no implementation tasks.
The first planning attempt blocks on the exact 1xx/3xx reachability question and issues no executable P work.

After the withheld supplement answers that question without changing accepted behavior, the Ready plan preserves O/B/D/C/S identifiers and supplies P items, dependencies, checkpoints, and completion evidence.
The readiness assessment is Ready, uses the accepted contract and current evidence rather than checklist completeness, and finds no unresolved implementation choice.
The verification report is Not Verified because the actual 429 branch contradicts the accepted retryable-response contract despite green reported tests.
Every transition observes its status gate; no later artifact is produced before explicit acceptance, and the scoped research detour does not reopen unaffected decisions.
Implementation occurs outside the pack; readiness and verification remain read-only and do not implement or repair the change.
